title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Aisha Rao
description: Summary: Implements a more robust automated detection pipeline for performance canaries and a configurable rollout guard that halts canary -> production promotion on statistically significant latency/throughput regressions. Motivation: we observed multiple small regressions that escaped the previous simple threshold detector because of noisy samples and no hysteresis. This PR adds a multi-stage detector (baseline window, canary window, bootstrap min-samples), percent-change + percentile-based checks, and hysteresis / cooldown so transient spikes do not incorrectly block rollouts. It also wires the detector into the rollout controller to perform automatic pause/rollback and annotates alerts with metric slices for faster debugging. Commits (high level): - Initial detector implementation and unit tests: perf-canary: add detector module with percentile comparison and bootstrap sampling (3 commits) - Integrate detector with rollout controller: wire canary-checks into the rollout state machine and add pause/rollback hooks (2 commits) - Controls/feature flags and config: expose new canary thresholds, min_samples, hysteresis_ms, and cooldown_window_ms as runtime config + CLI (1 commit) - Observability and dashboards: add tracing tags, canary result events to eventbus, and dashboard panels (1 commit) Changed areas (high level): - services/perf-canary/src/detector.py: new detector implementing baseline vs canary percentile comparisons, percent-change thresholds, sample size checks, and hysteresis state machine. - services/perf-canary/src/rollout_controller.py: integration points that call detector.check_canary() before promoting. Adds readable pause/retry reasons. - infra/helm/perf-canary/values.yaml: new default config keys (canary.thresholds, min_samples, hysteresis_ms, cooldown_window_ms). - observability/dashboards/perf_canary.json: panels for canary latency P50/P95, throughput, sample counts, and recent canary events. - tests/perf_canary/test_detector.py: unit tests covering edge cases (low-sample behavior, hysteresis, rollback path). - docs/perf_canary.md: user-facing doc on configuring rollout guards and interpreting canary events. - CI changes: new perf-canary unit + integration job that seeds synthetic traffic. Key behaviors and defaults: - Detection metric: by default compares P50 and P95 latency and requests/sec between baseline and canary windows. - Thresholding: regressions are flagged when percentile increases by more than the configured percent_change (default 12% for P50, 18% for P95) AND absolute delta exceeds a minimal latency delta to avoid tiny noise-based triggers. - Minimum statistical power: canary is ignored (treated as no-decision) if sample count < min_samples (default 100) or baseline count < min_samples. - Hysteresis & cooldown: when a regression is detected, a hysteresis window prevents immediate flip-flopping; the rollout controller will pause and wait for cooldown_window_ms (default 300_000ms) before re-evaluating. - Automatic rollback: if pause persists and aggregated metrics continue degrading for hysteresis_retries (configurable, default 3), the controller performs an automatic rollback and emits a high-severity alert. - False-positive mitigation: uses bootstrap-resampling of the sample windows to compute confidence on percent-change; only considers signals with >= default_confidence (0.9) to reduce noisy alerts. Backwards compatibility and config: all thresholds are configurable via helm values and runtime flags; defaults are conservative to avoid blocking normal rollouts. The previous boolean canary_strict mode remains supported. Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests added for detector edge cases and hysteresis transitions. - Integration test simulates baseline traffic and an injected latency-boosted canary to verify pause + rollback behavior. - Ran against perf-canary synthetic traffic harness in perf-lab for 24 hours to validate false-positive rate < 0.5% on stable workloads. Review conversation (abridged, chronological): - Priya: "Nice cleanup and good to see confidence-based checks. Please add a note about expected mean time added to rollouts in the docs (hysteresis/cooldown tradeoff)." - Aisha: "Added docs/perf_canary.md section about rollout time cost and examples of conservative vs aggressive configs." - Luca: "Can we reduce the default P50 threshold from 15% -> 12%? We saw a 13% regression earlier and it would've been useful to block it. Also add metric tags for model_id and region." - Aisha: "Lowered P50 to 12%, added model_id/region tags to emitted events and dashboards." - Diego (SRE): "What about low-sample canaries like quick canaries behind A/B flags? Make sure min_samples prevents noisy blocks." - Aisha: "min_samples remains configurable and defaults to 100. Added an explicit no-decision return and annotated the rollout UI to show sample counts so users understand why a decision wasn't made." - Priya (approve): "LGTM after CI green and docs updates." CI and merging: - First CI run: unit tests passed, integration job failed intermittently due to flakiness in the perf-harness; re-ran integration job with increased warmup and all checks passed. - CI summary: unit tests (pass), integration/perf-harness (pass on rerun), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). - Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-03-01. Release notes: "perf(canary): add enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards to detect latency and throughput regressions. New settings: canary.thresholds, min_samples, hysteresis_ms, cooldown_window_ms. Default thresholds tuned conservatively." Known limitations and follow-ups: - Does not currently support weighted traffic canaries where traffic is split per-minute; follow-up (ENG-3610) will add time-weighted aggregation and per-step checks. - Needs a UI affordance for manual override with an audit trail (ENG-3611). - Future: integrate canary detector outputs with Redwood Optimize signals for automatic model selection suggestions. release_notes: perf(canary): add enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards to detect latency and throughput regressions. New settings: canary.thresholds, min_samples, hysteresis_ms, cooldown_window_ms. Defaults are conservative to minimize false-positives.
